issue.title: Normalize legacy artifact created_at offsets to the configured timezone
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-em.5 while implementing epic sase-em (plans:202608/timezone_display_consistency.md); the epic plan explicitly deferred it to a separate task.

sase-em.5 changed src/sase/core/artifact_file_helpers.py::file_created_at to mint new artifact index rows with the configured-timezone offset, and the Rust core (sase-core e153a2e, released in 0.17.15) now buckets artifact calendar dates by the offset embedded in the RFC3339 created_at string. Artifact index rows written before that change still carry '+00:00', so they keep bucketing by the UTC calendar day.

Impact is bounded to calendar-day bucketing, not display: every display path already normalizes through sase.core.time.parse_local, and recency sorting uses the absolute instant, so both offsets render and order identically. Only 'sase artifact list --since'/'date:' filtering and retention age on legacy rows disagree with the day the row displays under, and only for rows created near the local midnight boundary (for America/New_York, anything minted 20:00-23:59 local).

The gap does not self-heal: src/sase/core/artifact_file_doctor.py::_backfilled_row (the 'sase artifact doctor --fix' path) fills only sha256, size_bytes, and mime_type, and never rewrites created_at, so an existing row is never re-derived from its file mtime.

Scope: add a one-shot, idempotent created_at normalization that re-derives the value from the stored file's mtime through file_created_at, skipping is_vcs_backed rows and rows whose stored path is missing (both already short-circuit in backfill_artifact_file_index). Decide whether it belongs in 'sase artifact doctor --fix' or a separately gated one-shot, since --fix is documented as enrichment-only and this rewrites an existing value. Cover a legacy '+00:00' row minted near the local midnight boundary and assert it buckets under the local day after normalization.
